{{Quote|Jem and I found this book in the Jedi Library on Ossus...|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="DEII6" />}}
This '''Jedi book''' was located in the [[Hall of Knowledge/Legends|Hall of Knowledge]] of [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Great Jedi Library]] on the planet [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]].<ref name="DEII4" /> It was written in an arcane<ref name="jvs" /> [[classical Ossan]] [[Language/Legends|language]],<ref name="EE2" /> with second chapter being authored by a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Thon]].<ref name="jvs" /> It described [[Force power/Legends|Force abilities]], including [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]].<ref name="DEII4" /> It also contained the stories of [[Arca Jeth]] of [[Arkania/Legends|Arkania]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Nomi Sunrider]].<ref name="EE2" />

This book was discovered by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Jem Ysanna]] in the subterranean ruins of [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Great Jedi Library]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]].<ref name="DEII4" /> In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]] on the course to the planet [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], assisted by [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[Vima-Da-Boda]] in translation of the book, learned ancient art of the [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]].<ref name="EE2" />

{{Book-stub}}

==Overview==
The book was written in an arcane<ref name="jvs" /> [[classical Ossan]] [[Language/Legends|language]],<ref name="EE2" /> and described [[Force power/Legends|Force abilities]], including [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]].<ref name="DEII4" /> It also contained the stories of [[Arca Jeth]] of [[Arkania/Legends|Arkania]], who freed [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] during the [[Beast Wars]], and of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Nomi Sunrider]], who learned battle meditation from Arca and [[Odan-Urr/Legends|two]] [[Thon|other]] masters.<ref name="EE2" />

The second chapter was authored by a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Thon]]:<ref name="jvs" />
{{ExcerptIU|
Why do scholars use the outcome of battles to indicate significant moments in history? Is not every moment significant in some way?

Why do analysts collect data about wars, counting the dead and wounded, and surveying the structures that survive? Do they really believe that if they collate such information, others will better understand why such events take place, and future wars might be prevented?

Then why—even now, as I write this—are so-called intelligent beings dominating and slaughtering others? Why are weapons still readied before peace is considered? Why are so many prepared to kill to achieve power, claim property, or prove that their gods are true?

The answer is simple: beings fight because they can, and sometimes because they must; sometimes by choice, but not always.

So long as there is life, there will be wars. Even the smallest insects can have their armies.

It is not the way of the Jedi to start wars.

It is the way of the Jedi to end wars, and to be aware that this duty is one that never ends.

Jedi battle meditation requires more from a Jedi than other disciplines. It can be most exhausting, and becomes even more challenging with the arrival of unexpected reinforcements for the opposition. But when it works, it works wonders.

If a Jedi's talent is measured by the ability to end battles without activating a lightsaber, then Jedi battle meditation must be counted among the most worthy of skills.
|attrib=The second chapter of the book
}}

==Behind the scenes==
The Jedi book first appeared in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity in [[Dark Empire II 4|''Dark Empire II'' 4]], a [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] written by [[Tom Veitch]], illustrated by [[Cam Kennedy]], and published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]<ref name="DEII4" /> on [[March 21]], [[1995]].<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54066/star_wars_dark_empire_ii_1994_4|text=Star Wars: Dark Empire II (1994) #4}}</ref> In the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], [[Luke Skywalker]] found ''[[Rammahgon]]'' in the subterranean ruins on the planet [[Ossus]].<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>
